rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a messenger has conclusively delivered the truth, continued disbelief brings certain destruction, by calamity or the believers’ sword.
rows.anchor: a nation to whom God’s sends a messenger is conclusively delivered the truth by Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger is the final means of conclusive communication, so the condemned nation receives no further respite.
rows.anchor: A messenger is the greatest, in fact, the final means of conclusive communication of the truth to its nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One aim of the fighting is to end religious persecution so nobody is harassed for accepting faith, regardless of status.
rows.anchor: This war should only end when their persecution ends: no one is harassed for accepting faith, whether he is rich or poor, free or slave.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other aim is that no religion besides Islam remain in the land of the House of God.
rows.anchor: The second objective is that in the land of the House of God no other religion except Islam remains.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The House was built for Abraham’s descendants and worship of the one God; Quraysh abandoned Abrahamic faith for idolatry and barred the Prophet’s community.
rows.anchor: The Quraysh, as pointed out earlier, never fulfilled these objectives and converted it into a place of idol worship.

rows.speaker: the Prophet (sws)
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that two religions cannot coexist in Arabia.
rows.anchor: two religions cannot exist together in the land of Arabia

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The directive concerns the territory around the House as well, since the sanctuary could be protected only by clearing the wider area of disbelief and polytheism.
rows.anchor: this directive was meant for the land in which the House of God was located

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Madinah also received sanctuary status from the Prophet, the command’s reach widened and non-Muslim elements were removed from the region around the House.
rows.anchor: Madī nah was also given this same status by Prophet Muḥammad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says Quraysh were first removed from the district, followed gradually by Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: the Jews and the Christians too were expelled from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conflict was about restoring the Abrahamic community’s right to the sanctuary: God sent the final messenger to complete the religion and make the House a source of guidance for the world.
rows.anchor: this House, in accordance with Abraham’s (sws) invocation, becomes a fountainhead of guidance and blessings for all the world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the opponents desist, God will forgive their past errors and judge only their future conduct, treating them according to its sincerity.
rows.anchor: God will not hold them accountable for their past mistakes. He will only take into account their future deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not fear the enemy’s numbers or weapons: God, their guardian and helper, does not disappoint those who turn to Him.
rows.anchor: believers should not be scared of the large weaponry and number of their enemy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah returns to the spoils question, explains their distribution as God’s plan rather than the Muslims’ own achievement, and calls for wholehearted acceptance.
rows.anchor: whatever they have obtained is because of God’s scheme and planning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming war instructions are presented as necessary for success and for distinguishing the motives of those who fight.
rows.anchor: These directives are essential to succeed in these wars

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Tawbah closes the Qur’an’s second chapter; Yūnus begins the third, which ends with al-Nūr, the only Madinan sūrah in the listed group of fourteen.
rows.anchor: Only the last one, Sūrah al-Nūr is Madīnan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter continues the paired-sūrah pattern; al-Nūr supplements al-Mu’minūn by completing the contrast between righteous and evil societies and stating God’s promise to believers.
rows.anchor: the traits of a righteous society are fully highlighted in comparison to an evil one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though some classify al-Ḥajj as Madinan, Islahi classifies it overall as Makkan by tone and content; a few later verses do not change a sūrah’s overall period.
rows.anchor: this opinion is not correct. Since the last sūrahs of this chapter were revealed very close to migration

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers resent a warning and glad tidings from one of their own and therefore call him a magician.
rows.anchor: Thus they regard him to be a magician.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is Lord and manager of creation; all return to Him, intercession requires His permission, and He justly rewards believers and punishes disbelievers.
rows.anchor: With full justice, He will immensely reward those who have professed faith and done righteous deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs in heaven and earth show that worldly life is not amusement; reflective people expect judgment, while the heedless face Hell and believers enter blissful gardens, rejoice, and thank God.
rows.anchor: Those who reflect believe that a day of justice will come after it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God delays punishment because He hastens mercy and lets rebels complete their wrongdoing and receive conclusive evidence; people plead in hardship, then forget God when respite comes.
rows.anchor: He shows haste in showing mercy but not so in sending His wrath.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past messengers’ histories warn the Quraysh; their generation has replaced earlier peoples as a test of its deeds and will not be treated differently.
rows.anchor: They have been actually raised up in their place in order to test them with regard to their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s demand for another book or edits is answered by the Prophet’s lack of authority to alter revelation; their imagined intercessors do not exist, and monotheism is God’s sole religion.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is that he is presenting before them God’s revelations and he does not have any right to amend them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s aversion to monotheism led them to demand a different book or changes to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: The aversion the Quraysh have for monotheism has induced them to demand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s long life among the Quraysh without a claim to prophethood supports Islahi’s point that he spoke only after God directed him.
rows.anchor: has never made any claim to prophethood or initiated preaching

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings imagined as intercessors do not exist; the Quraysh’s worship rests on figments of their imagination.
rows.anchor: the beings that they worship and think that they will intercede for them before God do not even exist

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent only monotheism, though people later created differences within this religion.
rows.anchor: The only religion He has sent to people is the religion of monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh demand a punishment sign, but only God controls whether it appears and when; their return to wrongdoing after respite shows why another sign will not help.
rows.anchor: The demand of the Quraysh for a sign of punishment is alluded to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly abundance is temporary: rain makes crops flourish and their owners imagine nobody can take them away, but God can suddenly destroy them.
rows.anchor: their owners think that who can deprive them of these.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone offers the abode of peace and guides the fortunate to it.
rows.anchor: The abode of peace is with God alone and He invites people to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fortunate receive radiant faces and Paradise, while those who earned evil are humiliated and cannot be saved from God.
rows.anchor: their faces will be as dark as the darkness of a dark night.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Last Day, disbelievers and the beings they worship will be separated, and the worshipped will disavow being worshipped.
rows.anchor: the disbelievers and those whom they worship will be distanced from one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Quraysh recognize God as creator, sustainer, and giver of life and death, they should recognize Him alone as Lord.
rows.anchor: they should also regard him to be their lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed deities have no share in creation, governance, or guidance, and conjecture cannot stand against the truth.
rows.anchor: These are mere conjectures which will be of no avail to them against the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s prophecies appear in earlier scriptures, which it confirms and explains.
rows.anchor: Its prophecies are found in the previous scriptures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who claim the Prophet fabricated the Qur’an are challenged to produce one sūrah like it, even with their deities’ help.
rows.anchor: ask them to bring a single sūrah like it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Judgment, each soul would ransom itself with all worldly treasure if possible, showing why deniers should not call for doom.
rows.anchor: every soul would like to redeem itself from the punishment by giving all the treasures of the world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promises to His friends are certain; honor is His alone, and those who worship other beings worship their own speculations.
rows.anchor: Those who worship others besides God only worship their speculations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of night and day belongs to God, and everything in heaven and earth is His; the supposed partners have no evidence and their worshippers face stern punishment.
rows.anchor: Those who have set up His partners out of their own desire do not have any proof for their existence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical accounts from Noah through Moses parallel the Prophet’s and companions’ opposition; steadfastness and trust in God lead to success for them and defeat for their opponents.
rows.anchor: the circumstances they are facing from his nation are the same as the ones faced by previous prophets

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment may arrive during the Prophet’s life or later, but a messenger’s nation is certainly judged in this world.
rows.anchor: It may come in the Prophet’s life time or it may descend later.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should disown those whose condition results from their own deeds; God has not wronged them.
rows.anchor: He should declare their acquittal from them. They have reached this state themselves because of their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a nation faces God’s law it no longer accepts faith; Jonah’s people were the exception, and believers should use intellect rather than wait for coercive punishment signs.
rows.anchor: When a nation faces God’s law, it does not accept faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could compel belief but chose not to; only people who reason and use insight accept faith, while spiritually filthy hearts remain unmoved by even great signs.
rows.anchor: Only they are willing to accept faith who use their intellect and insight.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to wait for the decisive punishment just as his deniers wait for it.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should tell tem to wait for it and he also will wait for it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s final declaration distinguishes his worship of the one God from the adversaries’ worship and commands him to remain with monotheism.
rows.anchor: he does not worship what they worship; he only worships the one and only God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits its recipient and misguidance harms its bearer; the Prophet delivered the truth and must follow revelation until God’s judgment.
rows.anchor: He who now accepts guidance will benefit from it and he who goes astray will bear its consequences.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers demand a punishment sign and promise faith if shown one, yet they remember God in calamity and return to evil after respite.
rows.anchor: as long as they are seized by a calamity that signifies such a sign, they keep God is remembrance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comfort and luxury do not place a people beyond God’s reach; punishment strikes when they are absorbed in affairs and think no danger is near.
rows.anchor: it thinks there is no danger for it from around it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh demanded a punishment sign, so the requested sign is contextualized as punishment rather than an ordinary portent.
rows.anchor: they demanded from him a sample of this vehemently proclaimed punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment warning challenged Quraysh’s arrogance and prompted demands to amend the Qur’an; the Prophet only conveys it, while God alone knows its timing and nature.
rows.anchor: it was not his prerogative to bring punishment. It is God Who has informed them of this punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s waiting reflects sorrow and yearning to save his people, not a wish for their punishment.
rows.anchor: This wait for him carries sorrow and yearning for his nation rather than any wish or desire for their punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general description of people refers to Quraysh and conveys divine aversion; leaders emerge from trials by inventing explanations that return their followers to negligence.
rows.anchor: Here the words used are general but they refer to the Quraysh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word makr means a hidden plot; one example is promising gratitude if delivered, then returning to rebellion.
rows.anchor: It refers to a hidden plot. One such plot hatched by the disbelievers against the signs of God is mentioned in the verse next verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another plot is the leaders’ historical philosophy that good and bad conditions happen to nations and therefore need not be read as warnings from God.
rows.anchor: against their own conscience their leaders in order to assure and comfort their followers state that such good and bad circumstances are encountered by nations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When used of God, makr means a hidden scheme; Islahi refers readers to his discussion of the term under Āl-i ʿImrān 3:54.
rows.anchor: it refers to a hidden scheme and I have

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s hidden scheme needs no delay and encompasses everyone; angels record the plots, and at the appointed time deniers are seized helplessly.
rows.anchor: All their deeds are being recorded by angels and nothing is hidden from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb tasīrūn means to set something in motion and here means embarking on a journey; travel means and ingenuity are gifts from God, so people should look beyond appearances.
rows.anchor: The word ﺗﺴﻴmeans “to set something in motion.” Here it refers to embark on a journey.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulk means ship and can be singular or plural, masculine or feminine; here its plural sense is indicated by the verb yajriin.
rows.anchor: Here it is use in the plural sense in the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase rīḥ ṭayyibah means favorable wind, contrasted with rīḥ ʿāṣif for a stormy wind.
rows.anchor: which is used for a stormy wind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shifts from direct to indirect address because indirect address suits a parable.
rows.anchor: In the earlier part of the verse, the address was direct; here it has become indirect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rebellious arrogance is unjustified for created beings who depend on the Creator’s mercy; it would suit only one sharing in creation and governance.
rows.anchor: such arrogance can only befit him who has a share in creation of this universe and its governance.
